content.summary: Welcome to Unit 10. In this reading mission, you will explore stories about people dealing with health issues, medical checkups, and recovery. You will practice identifying how past events connect using the Past Perfect grammar structures and essential health vocabulary.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Past Perfect Simple (had + past participle) and Past Perfect Continuous (had been + verb-ing) to show which past action happened before another.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Common health phrases such as take medication, make an appointment, feel sick, recover, and immune system.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning for chronological sequence words like when, before, after, and until to understand the order of past events.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas of short B1 texts about personal health and medical recovery.
Locate specific details regarding timelines using Past Perfect markers.
Recognize and apply health vocabulary in context correctly.

contextWarmup.prompt: What do you usually do first when you wake up with a sore throat and a high fever?
options: Make an appointment with a doctor and stay in bed
Go outside to play football immediately
Ignore it and eat lots of ice cream
contextWarmup.explanation: When you are sick with a fever and sore throat, the safest and healthiest choice is to rest in bed and make an appointment to see a doctor.

rules: Use the Past Perfect Simple (had + past participle) to talk about an action completed before another action in the past.
Use the Past Perfect Continuous (had been + verb-ing) to emphasize the duration of an ongoing action before another past action.
Use time linkers like when, as soon as, and until to connect past events clearly in your paragraphs.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Confusing Past Simple and Past Perfect
commonTrap.explanation: Learners often use the Past Simple for both past events, even when one clearly happened before the other.
commonTrap.wrong: By the time I arrived at the clinic, the doctor left.
commonTrap.correct: By the time I arrived at the clinic, the doctor had left.

paragraphs: Last winter, Mark had been feeling sick for almost two weeks before he finally decided to see a doctor. He thought the cough would disappear on its own, but it only got worse. By the time he made an appointment with the local clinic, his immune system had become extremely weak from lack of sleep and poor nutrition.

When the doctor examined him, she asked if he had been taking any medication. Mark admitted that he had only taken some herbal tea. The doctor prescribed proper medicine and advised him to rest. As soon as he started following her instructions, Mark began to get better and eventually managed to recover completely within ten days.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Past Perfect and Health Stories

content.summary: Practical guide on using the Past Perfect and health vocabulary to connect past events clearly in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Past Perfect Simple Formula
blueprintItems.example: She had already visited the doctor when the test results arrived.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Past Perfect Continuous Formula
blueprintItems.example: He had been exercising for an hour before he felt dizzy.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Using Time Linkers
blueprintItems.formula: Time linker + Past Simple clause, Past Perfect clause (or vice versa)
blueprintItems.example: As soon as I had taken my medicine, my headache started to fade.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize the pronoun 'I' and the first letter of every new sentence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i had a bad cold. when i woke up, my throat hurt.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I had a bad cold. When I woke up, my throat hurt.
mechanicsRules.why: The pronoun 'I' and sentence initial words must always be capitalized in English writing.

mechanicsRules.rule: Place a comma after an introductory time clause or linker phrase.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Before the doctor entered the room the patient had waited for an hour.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Before the doctor entered the room, the patient had waited for an hour.
mechanicsRules.why: Introductory dependent clauses need a comma to separate them from the main clause.

mechanicsRules.rule: Spell health terms correctly with proper spacing and hyphenation.
mechanicsRules.badExample: She suffered from a sorethroat and high bloodpressure.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: She suffered from a sore throat and high blood pressure.
mechanicsRules.why: Compound nouns like sore throat and blood pressure are written as separate words in standard English.

targetAnswers: By the time the trip started, he had caught a cold.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the affirmative sentence into the Past Perfect Simple:

practicumQuestions.hint: Change the time frame to past: By the time he went to sleep, he...
targetAnswers: By the time he went to sleep, he had taken his medicine.
He had taken his medicine before he went to sleep.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To shift this habit into a past completed sequence, use 'had taken' and past tense 'went'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct Past Perfect form of 'eat' and a time linker:

practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'had eaten' to show what happened before the stomachache.
targetAnswers: had eaten
practicumQuestions.explanation: The cause of the stomachache happened before the pain started, so the Past Perfect 'had eaten' is required.

practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize 'I', fix the contraction 'didn't', and check the phrasing.
targetAnswers: I didn't take my vitamins, so I caught a flu.
I didn't take my vitamins, so I had caught a flu.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The pronoun 'I' must be capitalized, 'didn't' requires an apostrophe, and clauses are joined properly with a comma before 'so'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a sentence using the Past Perfect Continuous and the health phrase 'exercise at the gym'.
practicumQuestions.promptText: Describe a long workout session before feeling tired.
practicumQuestions.hint: Example: He had been exercising at the gym for hours before he felt exhausted.
targetAnswers: He had been exercising at the gym for hours before he felt exhausted.
They had been exercising at the gym before they got tired.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The Past Perfect Continuous structure 'had been exercising' correctly highlights the duration of the action.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the sentences using 'until':
practicumQuestions.promptText: He stayed in bed. His fever went down completely.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'until' to show the duration of staying in bed.
targetAnswers: He stayed in bed until his fever had gone down completely.
He stayed in bed until his fever went down completely.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Until' indicates that an action continued up to a specific point in time when the other event occurred.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Health Habits and Past Experiences

content.summary: This speaking module focuses on discussing health habits and narrating medical events using the Past Perfect tense. Clear pronunciation of health terminology and accurate sentence stress help listeners understand the exact sequence of past health problems.
content.audioGuidance: Focus on linking auxiliary verbs like 'had' and 'had been' with main verbs. Pay attention to secondary stress in medical compounds like immune system and medication.

pillars.name: Auxiliary Reduction
pillars.explanation: In natural spoken English, 'had' is usually reduced to /həd/ or /əd/ when used as an auxiliary verb in the Past Perfect tense.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.target: Highlighting key health verbs and nouns
pillars.explanation: Stress content words such as 'doctor', 'medication', 'recover', and 'sick' while keeping grammatical words softer.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice how the primary stress shifts from the first syllable in medical to the third syllable in medication.
The stress moves to the penultimate syllable when changing from the verb recover to the noun recovery.
Prefix addition moves the primary stress to the final syllable in reappointment.
Stress shifts to the third syllable when moving from the adjective immune to the noun immunity.
